newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Vendex to sell KBB stake.
newsitem.headline: Vendex to sell KBB stake.

text.p: Retail and business services group Vendex International NV said on Tuesday it planned to sell its stake of about 36 percent in fellow Dutch retail group Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer NV (KBB).

Vendex said the shares would be sold in an international placement carried out by a syndicate led by Morgan Stanley and further consisting of ABN AMRO Rothschild, ING Barings and UBS. The placement is expected to be completed within two weeks.
A Vendex spokesman declined to comment on whether the placement would generate a book profit for Vendex and also declined to say how Vendex currently valued the stake.
KBB currently has some 11.8 million shares outstanding. The shares closed at 146.20 guilders each in Amsterdam on Monday.
Vendex said it had held a stake in KBB since the 1970s but no longer regarded it as a strategic investment.
It said that because there was little scope for cooperation between the two groups in the short term it had decided to sell the stake after discussing its plans with KBB.
KBB is a non-food retailer chiefly known for its Dutch department store chains De Bijenkorf and Hema.
It runs 248 chain stores and 1055 specialty stores, including the renowned New York toy store FAO Schwarz.
